overview.en: ITIS lists this as a valid species of the orthonectid genus Stoecharthrum.
overview.fr: ITIS reconnaît cette espèce comme valide dans le genre d’orthonectides Stoecharthrum.

identification.en: The original description reports specimens 300–365 μm long, with 40–46 epidermal cell rings.
identification.fr: La description originale rapporte des individus de 300–365 μm de long, avec 40–46 anneaux de cellules épidermiques.

habitat.en: It was found in Ascidia callosa from floating docks at Roche Harbor, Washington.
habitat.fr: Il a été trouvé chez Ascidia callosa sur des pontons flottants à Roche Harbor, dans l’État de Washington.

reproduction.en: The original study reports tightly grouped oocytes and sperm or its precursors in some specimens.
reproduction.fr: L’étude originale signale des ovocytes serrés et, chez certains individus, du sperme ou ses précurseurs.

ecology.en: Unlike S. fosterae in Mytilus trossulus, S. burresoni infects an ascidian and is shorter, with fewer cell rings and oocytes.
ecology.fr: Contrairement à S. fosterae chez Mytilus trossulus, S. burresoni parasite une ascidie et est plus court, avec moins d’anneaux cellulaires et d’ovocytes.

conservation.en: No species-level conservation assessment was found; the description is from one locality.
conservation.fr: Aucune évaluation de conservation propre à l’espèce n’a été trouvée ; la description vient d’un seul site.

title.en: Three new species of Stoecharthrum (phylum Orthonectida) — original description
title.fr: Three new species of Stoecharthrum (phylum Orthonectida) — description originale

facts: Kozloff's 1993 description reports the host, locality, measurements and comparison with S. fosterae.

budget.method: Complete referenced bilingual sentences and factual notes.

facts: ITIS records the species as valid in the orthonectid family Rhopaluridae.

budget.method: Complete referenced bilingual sentences and factual notes.

uncertainties: The original author examined very few parasitized ascidians and could not find further infected specimens; ecological prevalence is unknown.
review_note: Draft only; comparison with S. fosterae follows the original description and emphasizes the different hosts.
